headline: Multimodal and physics-aware graphs predict protein-ligand binding affinity
label: Ml Binding Affinity Screening
summary: Late-2025 reports pair multimodal fusion and physics-aware graph architectures with released tools for affinity-based compound ranking.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning that scores protein-ligand binding affinity or potency so candidate molecules can be ranked in screening workflows. kinCSM-RTK trains two models to predict pKi and pIC50 for small molecules against receptor tyrosine kinases and is released as a public web server. GIF-PLA fuses meta-path heterogeneous graphs of protein-ligand complexes with sequence and SMILES networks. MSPANet, a physics-aware graph network with KAN layers and radial and spherical basis encodings, predicts binding affinity and reports 8-12% gains. The ACaps-DDI capsule network applies self-attention to predict drug-drug interactions and is a neighboring application rather than an affinity model. What is new is the shift toward multimodal and physics-informed representations, with at least one model delivered externally.
